What is the MOQ for this wall mounted spice cabinet?

300 pieces per design. If you want more than one stain colour, each colourway counts toward the same 300 as long as the carcass is identical.

Yes. The carcass is built from flat stock, so width and height changes carry no tooling cost. Depth changes past about 18 cm start to affect carton efficiency, and we will flag that in the quote.

Yes. The shelf is 15 mm solid fir with a supported front edge, and the keyhole hangers are backed onto the rear rail rather than the panel. We pull-test the hangers on samples from each production run.

Assembled by default, because the joinery is part of the product's appeal. A knock-down version is possible if container efficiency matters more than out-of-box presentation on your market.

It is the classic nightstand organizer — the thing a man empties his pockets into — and it sells year-round as a gift and spikes hard for Father's Day and Christmas.

Key Features

  • Four defined compartments so a watch, wallet, keys and change each have a home instead of sharing one dish
  • Solid walnut, not veneer — the grain runs through the compartment walls, which is visible on the cut edges and is what buyers check
  • Shallow rounded wells with a hand-sanded interior so a watch case or phone back is never scratched
  • Felt or micro-suede base lining available in black, grey or cream to stop the tray sliding on a polished nightstand
  • Laser-engraved initials, monogram or brand mark on the rim or the base — per-unit cost, no plate charge, so single-name personalisation is practical
  • Flat-stacking form factor, so cartons ship dense and freight per unit stays low

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to men's gift and accessory brands, furniture and bedding retailers, department-store buyers, corporate-gift programmes and Shopify/Amazon home brands. Corporate gifting is the steadiest repeat volume, because an engraved walnut valet tray is one of the few desk-and-dresser gifts that survives a recipient's taste test; retail buyers order seasonally against Father's Day and Q4.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. On this tray the change buyers ask for most is the compartment map — a longer phone bay for a 6.7 in handset, or a dedicated slot for AirPods. Both are a jig change, not tooling, so there is no setup charge. Wood species swaps between walnut, oak and beech move the landed cost more than anything else you can specify.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can you change the compartment layout?

Yes. The divider positions are set by a jig, not by tooling, so a longer phone bay, a deeper watch well or a fifth compartment costs nothing extra to change — only the sample lead time.

Is it solid wood or veneer?

Solid walnut throughout, including the compartment walls. You can see it on the cut edges, which is exactly where buyers look. We can quote a veneered MDF version if you need a lower price point, but we would not call it walnut in your listing.

Can each unit be engraved with a different name?

Yes. Laser engraving is a per-unit operation with no plate or die cost, so a 300-piece order with 300 different monograms runs at the same unit price as 300 identical ones. Send the name list as a spreadsheet.

Do you offer hot foil stamping on the wood?

No. We do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood — neither bonds reliably to open grain, and the failure shows up weeks after delivery. Colour-fill laser engraving gives you a metallic gold, silver or copper mark that will not lift.

What is the carton and freight profile?

Trays nest flat, so a 300-piece order typically consolidates into a small pallet footprint. We send exact carton dimensions and gross weight with the quotation so you can price freight before you commit.

title: Leather-Lined Valet Tray — 4-Compartment Wooden Catchall for Keys, Watch and Wallet
content:
Introduction: A wooden valet tray with a leather lining: a hardwood body, four divided compartments, and a soft PU-leather skin across the base and compartment walls. It runs in two standing colourways — brown body with a cream lining, and black body with grey — and it is the version buyers choose when the tray has to sit on an entryway console and look like a finished accessory rather than a raw wooden dish.

  • PU-leather lining bonded across base and walls — quiet when keys drop in, and wipes clean
  • Two stock colourways: brown / cream and black / grey; other combinations on request
  • Hardwood carcass with a stained exterior, so the wood grain still reads on the outside faces
  • Non-slip base so it stays put on a lacquered console or a glass shelf
  • Debossed or foil-stamped logo on the leather — the one place on this product where foil does work

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to home and lifestyle retailers, men's accessory brands, hotel and serviced-apartment suppliers, and corporate-gift distributors. Hotels buy it for suite entryways and turndown service; gift distributors buy it because a logo debossed into leather photographs better in a catalogue than an engraving on bare wood.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Note the branding exception on this product: hot foil and debossing do work on the leather lining, even though we do not offer them on wood. If your logo needs a metallic finish, this is the tray to put it on. Lining colour, stitch detail and compartment layout are all open; genuine leather is quotable but roughly doubles the lining cost.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

You say you cannot foil on wood — can you foil this one?

Yes, because the mark goes on the leather, not the timber. Foil and deboss both hold on PU and genuine leather. On bare wood we still decline, and colour-fill laser engraving remains the metallic option there.

PU or genuine leather?

PU as standard — it is more colour-consistent across a 300-piece run and it survives humidity in transit better. Genuine leather is available and roughly doubles the lining cost; we will show you both on the sample if you are undecided.

Can we get a colourway that is not one of the two shown?

Yes. The two shown are simply what we have photographed. Lining colour has no tooling implication — send a swatch or a Pantone and we will match it on the sample.

Will the lining lift at the corners over time?

Not if the corners are relieved before bonding, which is the step cheap versions skip. We cut a relief at each internal corner so the leather folds rather than stretches. It is the single most common failure on this product category and it is a process control, not a material question.

Can it be made larger for a hotel entryway?

Yes. Give us the console depth you are fitting and we will size to it. Larger footprints usually drop one compartment and widen the others, which we will draw for you before sampling.

  • Laser engraving on the bamboo rim, or a printed logo on the silk

Wedding-favour and bridesmaid-gift sellers are the most reliable repeat buyers, because the shape photographs well and the engraved version carries a personalisation premium on a very low base cost.

Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Profile is the cheapest thing to change on this product — round, square, hexagonal and scalloped all run from the same setup. If you are building an assortment, taking three profiles with one silk colour costs less than one profile in three colours, because the dye lot is the expensive variable, not the cutter path.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Can we order more than one shape in the same PO?

Yes, and it is the cheaper way to build an assortment. Profiles run from the same setup, so three shapes at 100 each cost close to 300 of one shape. Silk colour changes are the variable that actually adds cost.

Moso bamboo is a grass that reaches harvest in four to five years against twenty-plus for hardwood, and our supply is plantation-grown. We can provide the mill documentation for your listing copy; we would not claim more than that.

title: Solid Walnut Catchall Tray — 3-Compartment 29x20 cm Entryway Key and Coin Organizer
content:
Introduction: A slim solid walnut catchall tray, 29 x 20 x 2 cm, routed from one board into three compartments. At 2 cm tall it is deliberately low — it reads as a surface, not as a container, which is why interior-led retailers pick this over a deeper valet box. It works equally as an entryway key tray and as a desk catchall next to a keyboard.

Key Features

  • 29 x 20 x 2 cm — low profile, so it disappears into a console or desk rather than dominating it
  • Routed from a single solid walnut board; no glued dividers, no joint lines to open up
  • Three compartments: one long, two short — keys, cards and coins
  • Oil-wax finish that can be refreshed by the end user rather than chipping like lacquer
  • Felt pads under each corner to protect the surface below
  • Engraving sits well on the wide flat rim; a full-width brand mark is legible here

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to design-led homeware retailers, museum and gallery shops, stationery and desk-accessory brands, and corporate-gift programmes. Gallery and museum shops are a particularly good fit: single-board walnut with a clean routed interior is the kind of object their buyers will list, and the flat rim takes an institution's name cleanly.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Because it is routed from one board rather than assembled, the compartment map is a CNC path — any layout you can draw, we can cut, at no tooling cost. The limits are the board: total footprint is capped by the walnut width we can source without a glue-up, and depth is capped at about 2.5 cm before the tray stops reading as slim. Tell us what has to fit and we will draw it.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why routed from one board instead of assembled?

Because glued dividers are where these trays fail. A glue line across the grain opens as the board moves with humidity, and it shows as a hairline crack after a season. Routing costs more in material waste and buys you a product that does not come back.

Can you cut a different compartment layout?

Yes, at no tooling cost — it is a CNC path. Send a sketch with the item you need each bay to hold and we will draw a layout and cut a sample.

How large can it go?

Footprint is limited by the widest walnut board we can source without a glue-up. Past that we can still build it, but it becomes a glued panel and we would tell you so rather than let you advertise single-board construction.

Is the oil finish durable enough for retail?

It is less scratch-resistant than lacquer but it is repairable — a customer can wipe on more oil and the mark disappears, which lacquer does not allow. For gift and design retail, oil is what buyers specify. For hospitality use we would recommend the lacquer version instead.

Can it be engraved with a long brand name?

Yes. The 2 cm rim runs the full 29 cm length, so a full wordmark fits legibly along the front edge. Colour-fill engraving in gold, silver or copper is available if you need it to read from a distance on shelf.

Can you size it to our own spice jars?

content:

No wooden caddy will, and anyone who tells you otherwise is selling you a replacement cycle. Ours is specified for wipe-down with sanitiser, which is how caddies are actually cleaned in service. We seal it for that and we say so plainly on the spec sheet.

Why does the handle matter so much?

Because it is the only part under repeated load. A glued dowel works loose after a few thousand lifts and the caddy is then binned. We through-tenon it so the joint carries the load mechanically, not just on glue.

Yes, and you should send the bottles or their exact diameter and height. Bay sizing is the one specification that cannot be fixed after tooling, and it is the most common reason a caddy order is rejected on arrival.

Yes. Per-unit engraving with no plate cost, so a 60-table restaurant gets 60 numbered caddies at the same unit price as 60 plain ones.

Yes. We hold the artwork and the spec after the first order, so a new site opening reorders against the same file with no re-sampling. Tell us at quotation stage if a rollout is coming and we will plan material batching for colour consistency across deliveries.

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why a slide instead of a hinge?

Because there is nothing to fail. A hinge is the component that loosens, a clasp is the component that corrodes, and both add cost and assembly steps. On a presentation box the slide also controls the pace of the unboxing, which is a large part of why the format is specified.

How tight should the lid be?

That is a decision you make at sampling and we set it in the groove depth. Too loose and it rattles in a courier bag; too tight and a customer struggles with it. We will send the sample with our recommended tension and you tell us which way to move it.

Can you make the insert?

Yes — die-cut foam, EVA, velvet-wrapped board or moulded paper pulp. Send us the actual product. Every insert problem we have ever had came from working off a drawing instead of the item.

Can we print full colour on the lid?

Yes, UV printing handles full colour on beech. For a metallic look, colour-fill laser engraving in gold, silver or copper is the option — we do not offer hot foil on wood because it does not bond reliably to grain.

What is the smallest order you will run?

300 pieces per design. Below that the setup cost per unit starts to dominate and you would be better served by a stock box with a printed sleeve, which we will tell you rather than take the order.

content:
Introduction: A wooden gift and keepsake box finished with full-colour UV printing. The ink is cured on contact by UV lamp, so it sits on the surface of the wood in full colour without soaking into the grain — which is what makes photographic artwork, gradients and brand colours possible on timber at all. There is no plate, no screen and no die, so a run of 300 with four artwork variants costs the same as 300 of one.

  • Scratch-resistant cured finish; can be over-coated with a matte or gloss lacquer for extra durability
  • Combines with laser engraving on the same box — printed colour plus an engraved tonal mark reads as expensive

Specifications

Sold to gift and stationery brands, subscription-box operators, wedding and event suppliers, corporate-gift distributors and licensed-merchandise companies. Licensed merchandise is the natural fit — artwork changes constantly, volumes per design are modest, and a printing process with no plate cost is the only way that maths works.

Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Send artwork as vector or at 300 dpi at final size, in CMYK. Two things to know before you design: wood is not white, so a light colour without a white underbase will shift warm — specify the underbase if colour accuracy matters; and grain texture shows through the print, which most buyers want and some do not. We will print both ways on the sample so you can see the difference rather than take our word for it.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will our brand colour print accurately on wood?

With a white underbase, close. Without one, it will shift warm because the wood tone shows through. If you have a strict brand colour, specify the underbase and send a Pantone reference; we will print a swatch strip on the sample so you approve the actual result, not a screen mock-up.

Can each box in the order carry different artwork?

Yes, at no additional cost. UV printing is digital — no plates, no screens. This is the reason to choose it over screen printing when you have more than one design.

Is the print durable?

The ink is UV-cured and bonded to the surface; it handles normal handling and wiping. For a box that will be carried daily or exposed to abrasion, we add a clear lacquer over the print, which we will quote as an option.

Can we combine printing with engraving?

Yes, and it is the single best-looking combination we offer. Colour print on the lid with a tonal engraved mark on the front or the base reads as a much more expensive box than either technique alone.

What file should we send?

Vector (AI, EPS, PDF) or 300 dpi at final size, CMYK, with fonts outlined. If you only have a logo as a low-resolution PNG we will tell you before sampling rather than print something soft and let you find out on delivery.

title: Slim Wooden Certificate Box — Sliding Lid Document and Award Presentation Case, Wholesale
content:
Introduction: A slim wooden certificate box with a sliding lid, built to hold a flat document — a diploma, a share certificate, an award citation, a warranty card or a set of prints. The depth is deliberately shallow so the box reads as a folio rather than a container, and the sliding lid means it opens flat on a desk without a hinge lifting the whole thing.

Sold to universities and professional bodies, awards and trophy suppliers, corporate recognition programmes, law and financial firms issuing share and title documents, and fine-art print sellers. Awards suppliers reorder annually against graduation and ceremony calendars, which makes them the most predictable volume in this category.

Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Give us the exact sheet size including any mount or backing board, and tell us whether the document goes in loose or in a sleeve — that changes the internal depth. A certificate box 1 mm under size is unusable, so we build the first sample around your actual document and send it back with the document in it if you post one to us.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. Frequently Asked Questions

Can you size it to our certificate exactly?

Yes, and we would rather work from the physical document than from a nominal paper size. Certificates are frequently trimmed, mounted or backed, and the finished sheet is often not the size the paper spec says.

How does the document come out without bending?

Either a ribbon loop under the sheet that you lift, or a semicircular notch machined into the base so a finger can get underneath. The ribbon is better for a mounted certificate, the notch for a loose sheet. We will recommend one for your document.

Can we have our crest on the lid?

Yes. Laser engraving for a tonal mark, colour-fill engraving for gold or silver, or UV printing for full colour. Institutional crests with fine linework engrave beautifully; we will send a test engraving of your crest at size before you commit.

It is designed to. The flat profile means it goes into a standard mailing carton without a bespoke pack, and the sliding lid does not spring open in transit the way a hinged lid can.

Can you do a matching folder or a larger box for a set?

Yes — we regularly build a family: a certificate box, a deeper award box and a matching pen box in the same timber and finish. Batching them in one order also keeps the colour consistent, which is hard to guarantee across separate runs.

title: Walnut Coin Display Box with Acrylic Lid — Collector Coin and Medal Presentation Case
content:
Introduction: A walnut coin display box with a clear acrylic lid, so the collection is visible without being handled. The interior is a velvet or flocked insert with wells cut to your coin, capsule or medal diameter. It is a collector and mint product: the acrylic lid exists because the whole point is to look at the coins, and every time one is picked up it loses condition.

Key Features

  • Clear acrylic lid — the collection is displayed without handling, which is what protects grade
  • Wells cut to your capsule diameter, not to a generic coin size; capsules vary and a loose well lets a coin move
  • Velvet or flocked insert in navy, black, burgundy or your colour
  • Solid walnut carcass with mitred corners — the visual weight collectors expect
  • Single-layer or stacked-tray configurations for larger collections
  • Engraved lid frame or base plate for a mint's name, an issue title or a year

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to mints and commemorative-coin issuers, numismatic dealers and auction houses, military and civic medal suppliers, and collectible retailers. Commemorative issues are the best fit because each release needs its own box with its own engraved title, and per-unit engraving means that costs nothing extra.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Send a capsule, or the exact outer diameter and thickness of the capsule you use — not the coin. Almost every fit problem in this category comes from someone specifying a 38.6 mm coin and receiving a box that will not take the 44 mm capsule it lives in. Well depth matters as much as diameter: the coin should sit proud enough to lift out but not touch the acrylic.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Should we send you the coin or the capsule?

The capsule, always, or its exact outer diameter and thickness. Coins are specified by their own diameter and the capsule is considerably larger. This is the single most common specification error in the category.

Will the coin touch the acrylic?

Not if the well depth is right, and we set it so there is clearance. A coin pressing against the lid is how a display box damages the thing it is protecting, so we check it on the sample with your actual capsule in place.

Can we have stacked trays?

Yes, for larger collections. Two or three trays lift out on ribbon pulls with the acrylic lid over the top. Beyond three the box gets deep enough that we would suggest a drawer format instead, which we also build.

Can each box be engraved with a different issue title and year?

Yes — per-unit laser engraving, no plate cost. Mints typically reuse one box design across an annual programme and change only the engraved line, which is exactly what this process is good for.

Is acrylic or glass better here?

Acrylic, for a box that gets posted. Glass is heavier, adds packing cost and is the component that arrives broken. If you specifically want glass for a premium presentation piece we will build it, and we will tell you what it does to your damage rate.

title: Rustic Hinged Wooden Keepsake Box — Memory Box with Brass Clasp, Wholesale
content:
Introduction: A rustic wooden keepsake box with a hinged lid and a brass clasp — the familiar memory-box format, built properly. The rustic look comes from the timber and the finish, not from sloppy joinery: corners are square, the lid sits flush, and the clasp is aligned so it closes with one hand. If you are a personalisation seller, buy it blank and we will optimise the lid for your laser — a slightly flatter, more uniform lid face engraves more evenly than a heavily distressed one, and we can supply either. If you want us to engrave, send the name list as a spreadsheet; per-unit engraving carries no plate cost. Hardware finish, interior lining and size are all open.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can we buy these blank for our own engraving?

Yes, and many of our buyers do. Tell us you are engraving in-house and we will specify a flatter, more uniform lid face and a lighter stain, both of which give you a cleaner and more consistent burn than the heavily distressed finish.

Will the clasp line up?

It does on ours, because the clasp is located from a fixture rather than by eye. A clasp that needs the lid pressed sideways to catch is the defining defect of this product category, and it is a process control, not a cost question.

What timber gives the most rustic look?

Pine and paulownia take a rustic stain best because their grain is open and the colour variation is part of the effect. Beech looks cleaner and more contemporary. We will send both on the sample if you have not decided.

Can we have a lift-out tray inside?

Yes — a shallow tray on ledges with a finger notch or ribbon. It is a good upsell on a memory box because it turns one compartment into two without changing the outside.

300 per design. If you need several sizes, note that a size change is a cheap change — three sizes at 100 each is close in cost to 300 of one, so building an assortment does not cost what buyers usually assume.

content:
Introduction: A wooden keepsake box with a fully laser engraved lid — mandala geometry or a perpetual-calendar face as shown, and any artwork you send in place of either. Wellness and spiritual brands are the strongest fit for the mandala design specifically; the perpetual-calendar lid sells into desk-accessory and corporate-gift channels instead.

Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Send artwork as vector with a single stroke weight if you can — engraving reproduces line art far better than it reproduces photographs, and a design drawn for print often needs redrawing for a laser. We will do that redraw as part of sampling. Timber choice changes the look more than anything else: pale beech and birch give high contrast, walnut gives a subtle tonal mark that needs a colour fill to read across a shop.

Can you engrave our own artwork instead?

Yes, and at the same price. Vector line art works best. If you send a photograph or a raster logo we will redraw it for engraving during sampling and show you the result before you approve.

Does the design cost more if it is complicated?

No. It costs more machine time, which is a small part of the unit cost, and there is no plate or die at all. This is the reason to choose engraving over screen printing for detailed work.

Which wood shows the engraving best?

Beech and birch ply give the highest contrast because the burn is dark against a pale surface. Walnut gives a subtle, expensive-looking tonal mark, but it needs a gold or silver colour fill to read from more than a metre away — worth knowing if the box has to sell off a shelf.

Will the engraving wear off?

No. It is a burn into the timber, not a coating. That is the practical argument for engraving over printing on any product that gets handled daily.

Can every box carry a different design?

Pillow circumference is the specification that decides whether the box works. Send us a watch — a 44 mm diver on a rubber strap and a 36 mm dress watch on leather need different pillows, and a box sized for one holds the other badly. Glass or acrylic lid?

Will it fit large watches?

Can we get our logo inside?

Introduction: A solid walnut watch box with a glass lid — the natural-timber alternative to a lacquered case, for buyers who want the grain visible rather than hidden under gloss. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Solid walnut is the constraint and the selling point at once: board width caps the box size before we have to glue up a panel, and we will tell you when a size you want crosses that line rather than let you advertise solid construction on a laminated panel. Is it solid wood or veneer?

Solid walnut. Look at the mitred corners: on solid construction the grain runs continuously around the corner, and on a veneered carcass it stops. It is the check every collector makes and it is why we build it this way.

Oil or lacquer finish?

Oil for an open-pore, natural feel that the owner can refresh; satin lacquer for more scratch resistance and a slightly more uniform tone. For a box that will sit on a dresser and be handled, oil ages better; for retail display, lacquer holds up to handling by strangers.

Can you grain-match a set?

Yes, if the order is batched. Cutting lid and body from adjacent boards is standard on ours; matching across a whole order needs the timber reserved at the start, which we do if you tell us at quotation stage.

How large can it go in solid walnut?

Until we would have to glue up a panel to reach the width. We will tell you exactly where that line falls for your dimensions. Past it we can still build the box, but it is a laminated panel and you should not describe it as single-board.

Can the lining be a brand colour?

Yes, velvet or suede to a Pantone. Note that on a natural-wood box the lining is the only strict-colour element; the timber itself varies board to board, which is the nature of the material and part of what buyers are paying for.

Do all four slot counts cost the same to tool?

There is no separate tooling — they run on the same construction with a different body length and partition count. That is why this model is the sensible choice for building a price-laddered assortment.

Can we buy it blank for our own engraving?

Yes. Tell us and we will supply the lighter, flatter lid variant, which burns far more evenly than the distressed finish. It is the same price.

How large a watch will the slots take?

Send us a watch. The standard pillow suits a typical 38–42 mm case; for chunky divers we will increase the pillow circumference and, if needed, the internal height. Pillows are cheap to change and impossible to change after the order ships.

Glass as standard. On a lower-price model acrylic is a legitimate cost saving and we will quote it; be aware it scratches in normal use and on a display box the scratches are the first thing a customer sees.

Is the rustic finish consistent across an order?

Within the normal variation of a stained natural timber, yes — and some variation is the point of a rustic finish. If you need tight consistency for a retail shelf line-up, we would steer you to the lacquered model instead and say so.

Is this a safe?

No. It is a wooden cabinet with a cam lock. It deters casual access and stops a lid being opened by a guest or a child. It is not a security device, it will not resist a determined attempt, and we will not let it be described as one.

content:
Introduction: A bamboo watch box for a single watch, with a rustic natural finish and a fitted pillow. It is the sustainable-materials answer in this category: bamboo is a fast-renewing grass, it takes an engraving beautifully, and it lets a brand make a credible environmental claim about its packaging without moving to cardboard and losing the object.

  • Light, so the freight cost per unit is lower than an equivalent hardwood box

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to sustainable and eco-positioned watch brands, wooden-watch makers, gift retailers and marketplace sellers. Wooden-watch brands are the obvious fit — a bamboo box is the only packaging that does not undercut the product's own story — and they reorder with every collection.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. If the sustainability claim is part of your marketing, be careful what you specify around it. A heavy stain, a plastic insert or a foil label all weaken the claim. We would put an engraved mark on unstained bamboo with a paper-based insert and a recycled outer, and we can supply the mill documentation to support what you write in your listing.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is bamboo a defensible environmental claim?

It is a grass that reaches harvest in four to five years and our supply is plantation grown. We can provide mill documentation for your copy. We would not let you claim more than that, and we would advise against pairing it with a plastic insert, which undoes the argument.

Does bamboo engrave well?

Better than most hardwoods — the burn goes noticeably darker against the pale surface, so a logo reads strongly with no ink. It is the main practical reason brands choose bamboo for a branded box over a stained pine.

Will it warp in a humid market?

Not if the moisture content is right at packing, which is why we measure it twice and state it on the packing list. Bamboo is dimensionally more stable than most solid hardwoods, which helps, but the kilning discipline is what actually decides it.

Can we have it in a dark finish?

Carbonised bamboo gives a warm dark tone through heat treatment rather than stain, which keeps the material story clean. A stained version is available and we would flag what it does to your sustainability claim before you commit.

Is it cheaper than hardwood?

Usually, and the freight is lower because it is lighter. The gap is smaller than buyers expect on a small box where labour dominates; ask us to quote both against your spec rather than assuming.

Because the pieces have to fit each other. The most common failure we see is a presentation box bought from one supplier and a carton from another, with 4 mm of slack that turns into a crushed corner in transit. One specification removes that risk and one lead time removes the waiting.

On the lining and the closure. Those are what the customer touches and hears. Timber species changes the photograph more than the experience, and we will tell you honestly when a walnut upgrade is not worth what it costs you.

Sold to kitchenware and gourmet-food retailers, cheese and deli brands, wedding and housewarming gift sellers, and promotional-product distributors. Cheese and deli brands are the natural attachment: a branded slicer sold alongside the product is a recurring reminder of who to buy the cheese from.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Wire gauge is the specification worth discussing. A finer wire cuts hard cheese more cleanly; a heavier wire survives a careless user on a cold block. We will supply whichever you specify and we will tell you which complaint each one generates. Board size, engraving and whether spare wires ship inside the retail pack are all open.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can the wire be replaced by the customer?

Yes, and spares ship with each unit. A wire cutter whose wire cannot be replaced is a disposable product, and we would not build it that way. Make sure your retail pack says so on the outside — it is a selling point most competitors bury.

What cheeses does it handle?

Hard and semi-soft blocks — cheddar, gouda, gruyere, halloumi. Very soft and very crumbly cheeses are not what a wire is for, and it is better to say so in your listing than to take the return.

What wire gauge do you recommend?

Finer for a cleaner cut on hard cheese; heavier if you expect the product to be used carelessly on cheese straight from the fridge. Both are available. We will tell you which failure mode each choice buys you.

Is bamboo suitable for a cutting surface?

For cheese, yes — it is dense, dimensionally stable and sealed food-safe. It is harder on knife edges than end-grain hardwood, which matters for a chopping board and does not matter here, because the cutting is done by a wire.

Is it good as a promotional gift?

It is one of the better ones in kitchen. The engraved board face is large and flat, the unit cost is low, and unlike most promotional items it gets used in front of guests. Per-unit engraving means no plate cost even on a few hundred.

title: Rattan Inlay Wooden Serving Tray — Nested Set of 3 Hotel and Restaurant Trays
content:
Introduction: A dark-stained wooden serving tray with a woven rattan panel set into the base, supplied as a nested set of three sizes. The weave is the point: it gives grip so a cup does not slide when the tray is carried, and it reads as craft rather than as a flat board. It is a tea-house and hotel service tray first, and a styling tray for retail second.

Key Features

  • Woven rattan panel base — cups and glasses grip the weave instead of sliding on lacquer
  • Nested set of three: three sizes ship in the footprint of the largest, which is what makes the freight economics work on a tray set
  • Mitred hardwood frame with a rebated panel, so the weave sits flush and nothing catches a cloth
  • Dark walnut-tone stain with a sealed finish that survives daily wiping in service
  • Raised rim on all four sides, low enough that a hand can still pick up a cup at the edge
  • Panel is replaceable — a worn weave can be changed without scrapping the frame

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to hotel and F&B procurement, tea and coffee houses, catering-equipment distributors, and homeware retailers building a natural-materials range. Tea houses and specialty coffee are the natural fit — the weave suits their material language and the grip solves a real service problem that a plain lacquered tray does not.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Two things drive the spec: the largest item the tray has to carry, and whether it is carried one-handed. One-handed service needs a narrower tray than most buyers first ask for. The rattan panel can be swapped for woven bamboo or seagrass at no tooling cost, and a darker or paler stain changes the whole character for nothing.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Does the weave come loose over time?

Not when the panel is rebated into the frame rather than glued onto the base, which is how we build it. A surface-glued weave lifts at the edges within months of being wiped. Ask any supplier you are comparing whether the panel is rebated.

Can it be wiped with sanitiser?

Yes — the frame is sealed for it. The weave itself should be wiped rather than soaked; we will say so on the care sheet that ships with the sample so your customers are not surprised.

Can we order one size instead of the set?

Yes. The set exists because it ships efficiently and merchandises well, but single sizes are quoted the same way. If you are a hotel buying for one service format, a single size is usually the right call.

Is the panel really rattan?

Rattan on the standard build. Bamboo and seagrass weaves are available and cost slightly less. We will send you all three on the sample rather than describe the difference, because it is a texture decision and photographs badly.

Can we brand it?

Laser engraving on the wooden frame is the clean option. A woven-in or printed mark on the panel is possible but it sits under the cups and gets hidden in use, so we would steer you to the frame.

title: Rustic Wooden Tray with Glass Base — Nested Decorative Serving Tray Set of 3
content:
Introduction: A rustic wooden frame tray with a textured glass base, in a nested set of three sizes. The glass is what sells it: it wipes completely clean where bare wood stains, it catches light in a way timber cannot, and it lets the tray work for wet items — perfume, oils, cocktails — that would mark a plain wooden board.

Specify tempered glass, and insist on it from any supplier — an untempered panel in a carried tray is a safety problem, not a cost saving. Base options are textured, clear, smoked and mirror; mirror is the most requested for vanity and perfume merchandising and costs a little more. Frame finish and size are open.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is the glass tempered?

Yes, and we would not build it otherwise. A tray is picked up and carried; annealed glass that breaks in a fall produces long shards, tempered glass does not. If a quote you are comparing is much cheaper, this is the first thing to check.

Can we have a mirror base instead?

Yes, and it is the most requested variant for vanity, perfume and cocktail merchandising. It costs a little more and shows fingerprints, which is worth knowing before you commit a whole range to it.

Will the glass rattle in the frame?

No — it sits on a silicone bed rather than directly on timber. That also stops a knock transmitting straight into the panel edge, which is where a glass base cracks.

Can the tray go in a dishwasher?

No. The frame is wood. Wipe-clean only, and we put that on the care sheet with the sample so it reaches your end customer rather than getting lost between us.

Can the glass be printed?

Yes — frosted etching or ceramic print. Frosting a logo into the corner of the panel looks expensive and survives cleaning; printed colour on glass is more fragile under repeated wiping and we will tell you so.

content:

title: Carved Lattice Wooden Gift Box — Silk-Lined Pine Box with Window and Rope Handle
content:
Introduction: A pine gift box with a carved lattice window on each face, a silk lining, an antique-brass clasp and a rope carry handle. The lattice is a fretwork cut, not a printed panel — light passes through it and the contents show, which is the whole point of a window box. Specifications

Sold to tea and Chinese-medicine brands, spirits and baijiu producers, moon-cake and festival gift packers, and giftware retailers. Festival gifting is the volume: a box that shows the product through a carved window and carries by a rope handle is exactly the format that seasonal gift programmes reorder every year.

Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. The lattice is the thing to make yours. It is a cutter path, so replacing our pattern with your own motif — a brand mark, a regional pattern, a seasonal design — costs nothing beyond the drawing. Very fine lattice weakens the panel, so send us the design and we will tell you where it needs thickening before we cut a sample rather than after.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. Frequently Asked Questions

Can we use our own lattice pattern?

Yes, at no extra cost — it is a cutter path, not tooling. Send vector artwork. If any part of your pattern is too fine to hold together in pine, we will tell you before cutting and show you the minimum web thickness.

Is there glass behind the window?

A clear acrylic insert as standard, because these boxes get carried and posted. Glass is available if the box will sit on a shelf rather than travel, and we will quote the difference including what it does to your damage rate.

Which finish sells better?

The torched burnt-oak reads as more premium and photographs better on a dark background; natural pine is brighter on a retail shelf and cheaper. Most festival programmes take the torched version. We will send both on the sample.

Can the silk be a brand colour?

Yes. Gold is stocked; other colours need a dye lot with a small first-run surcharge, and repeat orders in the same colour carry no surcharge.

It can, with a fitted insert. Tell us the bottle and we will cut foam or a wooden cradle to it. Without an insert a bottle will move in transit and the lattice panel is the part that breaks.

title: Vintage Leather Wine Bottle Box — Single Bottle Wooden Case with Handle and Clasp
content:
Introduction: A single-bottle wine box in the antique trunk style: a curved wooden carcass wrapped in aged burgundy leather, with a woven-texture panel, brass studs, a swing clasp and a stitched leather carry handle. It is deliberately not a clean modern box — it is bought for the theatre, and it sells to people giving a bottle as an occasion rather than as a drink.

Key Features

  • Aged leather wrap with a woven-texture inset panel and antique-brass studs

  • Swing clasp with an aligned catch; lined interior cradles the bottle
  • Colour options in burgundy, tan, dark brown and black
  • Deboss or foil on the leather — the one material in our range where foil bonds reliably

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to wine and spirits brands, duty-free and travel retail, corporate-gift distributors, and gift retailers. Corporate gifting is the steady volume because a debossed logo on aged leather is one of the few marks that looks more expensive than it costs, and the format survives being posted.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Send us the bottle. Bordeaux, Burgundy and sparkling profiles are all different diameters and shoulder heights, and a cradle cut for one holds another badly. On branding, this is the product where foil and deboss work, because the mark goes into leather rather than into open wood grain — if your logo needs a metallic finish, put it here.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Frequently Asked Questions

Will the handle hold a full bottle?

Yes — it is riveted through the carcass, not glued to the leather skin. A handle bonded to the covering is the failure on cheap versions of this box, and it fails while someone is carrying a gift, which is the worst possible moment.

PU or genuine leather?

PU as standard; it is more colour-consistent across a run and holds up better in humid transit. Genuine leather is available at roughly double the covering cost and we will put both on the sample if you are choosing.

Can you fit a champagne bottle?

Yes, with a different carcass — sparkling bottles are wider and taller than a standard Bordeaux. Tell us at quotation which profile you are packing, or send a bottle.

Can the logo be gold?

Yes. Hot foil works on leather, which is the exception in our range — we do not offer foil on bare wood because it does not bond to grain. Deboss with a gold foil fill is the most popular finish here.

Does it ship well?

With the right outer carton, yes, and the curved profile is actually more knock-tolerant than a square box because there are no corners to crush. We specify the shipper alongside the box.

title: Whiskey Stones Gift Set Box — Walnut Case with Glass, Chilling Stones and Tongs
content:
Introduction: A walnut-faced hinged box holding a complete whiskey stones gift set: nine chilling stones, a crystal-cut tumbler and stainless tongs, all seated in a fitted foam bed with a moulded lid pad. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. The glass is the risk and the lever at once. A heavier cut tumbler lifts the perceived value noticeably and raises your breakage rate unless the foam is right, which is why we mould the lid pad rather than leaving a gap above the glass. Tell us your target retail and we will tell you which glass gets you there; we would rather do that than have you discover it after tooling.

Frequently Asked Questions

Do the stones actually chill?

They cool without diluting, which is the claim worth making, and they do not chill as hard as ice. We would write it that way in your listing. Overclaiming on this product is the reliable route to returns.

How do you stop the glass breaking in transit?

A die-cut foam bed under it and a moulded pad in the lid, so the glass is trapped on both faces. Most sets on the market foam only the base and leave a void above; that void is where the breakage comes from.

Can we change what is in the set?

Yes — second glass, different tumbler shape, more or fewer stones, add a slate coaster. Each change means a new foam cut, which is cheap, so build the set you want rather than the one we photographed.

Food-safe soapstone, washed before packing. We can supply the material test report for your listing and for customs if your market asks for it.

What is the lead time for a Christmas programme?

Sampling 14–18 days, production 35–45 days, then freight. Work backwards from your in-store date and add a fortnight of slack; for Q4 that usually means committing in spring.

title: Mr and Mrs Wedding Keepsake Box — Engraved Sliding Lid Wooden Memory Box
content:
Introduction: An ash wedding keepsake box with a sliding lid engraved “mr & mrs”. The lid runs in a machined groove with no hinge and no hardware, which is what lets the engraving run edge to edge across an uninterrupted face. It is a wedding-gift product and it lives or dies on personalisation: names, dates, vows, coordinates.

Key Features

  • Machined slide groove, tuned so the lid moves smoothly without falling out
  • Interior plain or felt-lined; a divided insert is available for rings, cards and a garter
  • Ships flat-lidded, so the engraved face is protected in transit

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to wedding and event suppliers, personalisation and print-on-demand sellers, gift retailers, and marketplace brands. Personalisation sellers are the best customers here: they buy blanks at volume, engrave to order in their own market, and reorder on a short cycle because the inventory turns fast.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. If you engrave in-house, buy it blank and tell us — we will supply a flatter, more uniformly sanded lid than the display version, which gives your laser a cleaner and more repeatable burn. If we engrave, send names as a spreadsheet with exact spelling and accents. Ash gives the most contrast; walnut looks richer but needs a colour fill to read on a shelf.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Can every box have different names and a different date?

Yes, and that is the reason to choose laser over print here. There is no plate, so the file changes and nothing else does. Send a spreadsheet; we will proof the first ten back to you before running the batch.

Can we buy them blank to engrave ourselves?

Yes, and many of our buyers do. Say so at order and we will supply the flatter-sanded lid variant at the same price — it burns more evenly than the finished display version.

Which wood engraves best?

Ash and beech give the highest contrast because the burn is dark against a pale surface. Walnut looks more expensive but the mark is tonal and needs a gold or silver fill to read from across a room, which is worth knowing if it has to sell off a shelf.

Can the artwork be something other than mr & mrs?

Yes, at no extra cost. Anniversary, baby, graduation, pet memorial — same box, different file. Several of our buyers run one box body across four seasonal artwork lines.

Will the lid fall out?

Not at the tension we set, and you approve that tension on the sample. Too loose and it slides out in a gift bag; too tight and a customer struggles. We will send it at our recommended setting and move it either way on your word.

  • Kiln-dried pine at controlled moisture, so the slats do not cup in a container
  • Dividers optional: bottle-to-bottle contact is fine for a crate, and not for a gift

Specifications

Sold to wineries and cellar-door retail, hamper and gift-basket companies, wine importers and subscription clubs, and prop and display buyers. Hamper companies are the largest repeat volume because the crate doubles as the presentation and the shipper, which removes a whole packaging line from their cost.

Decide early whether the crate ships loaded or ships empty to be packed. A crate that travels with bottles in it needs dividers and a heavier slat section; one that is packed at the destination does not, and paying for the heavy version when you do not need it is the most common overspend in this category. Can it ship with bottles inside?

Yes, but specify it that way. A loaded crate needs dividers and a heavier slat section than one that gets packed at the destination. Tell us which at quotation and we will build the right one rather than the cheap one.

Can we print our own vineyard artwork?

Yes — screen print on the slats, one or two colours, with a screen cost on the first run and none on reorders. Laser engraving is the alternative and costs per unit with no setup, which is better below about 500 pieces.

Will the slats warp?

Not at 8-12% moisture content, which we measure after kilning and again before packing and state on the packing list. Slatted crates are more exposed to this than solid boxes because every slat is free to move, which is exactly why we control it.

Is the pine treated for export?

Kiln-dried and compliant for the usual destinations. Tell us your import market at quotation and we will confirm the treatment and marking your customs authority requires, in writing, before you ship.

Can we get 12 bottles?

Yes, and 3. Twelve gets heavy enough that we would move the rope handles to reinforced anchors, which we will quote. Three is the best-selling gift size after six.

This is the cost-efficient six-bottle format, and that is the honest reason to choose it over the slatted crate: fewer parts and no hardware. The pulp insert is also the right call over wooden dividers for most buyers — it protects better, weighs less and recycles, and it costs less. Pulp inserts or wooden dividers?

Pulp for most buyers — it protects better, weighs less, recycles, and costs less. Take wooden dividers only when the box is displayed open and empty on a shelf, where the pulp reads as cheap.

How big is the printable area?

The full lid, edge to edge, because there is no hinge or catch breaking it up. That is the main reason this format is chosen over a hinged box for own-label work.

Screen for one or two flat colours at volume — cheaper per unit, with a one-off screen cost. UV for full-colour artwork or several designs, because there is no plate at all. We will tell you the crossover point for your quantity.

In the shipper, yes. On its own, a sliding lid can walk if the box is stood on end, so we set the groove tension for a firm fit and we specify the outer carton with the box rather than leaving it to you.

title: Plain Wooden Crate with Rope Handle — Unfinished Paulownia Box with Hinged Lid
content:
Introduction: An unfinished paulownia crate with dovetailed corners, a hinged lid, twin brass clasps and a rope carry handle. It is deliberately plain: no print, no stain, no lining. This is the blank that personalisation sellers, craft retailers and gift packers buy by the pallet, because everything they want to do to it is easier on bare wood than on a finished box.

Sold to personalisation and print-on-demand sellers, craft and hobby retailers, gift packers and hamper companies, and wedding suppliers. Print-on-demand is the volume buyer: they need a consistent blank in quantity, and consistency of sanding and colour across a run matters more to them than any feature.

If you are engraving or printing, tell us and we will hold the sanding grade and batch the timber for colour — paulownia varies more board to board than buyers expect, and a pallet of blanks that engrave to three different tones is a real problem for a seller listing one photograph. Size, hardware finish and species are all open.

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. Frequently Asked Questions

Why unfinished?

Because everything a personalisation seller wants to do works better on bare wood. Stain takes evenly, laser burns cleanly, vinyl sticks, decoupage bonds. A sealed box has to be sanded back first, and that is labour you would be paying for twice.

Will the boxes match each other in colour?

Within paulownia's natural variation as standard. If you are listing one photograph against a whole run, ask us to batch the timber for colour — we can hold it much tighter and it costs a little more. It is worth it for marketplace sellers.

Why paulownia rather than pine?

Weight. Paulownia is substantially lighter for the same strength, which you feel when the box is carried and pay for when it is freighted. Pine is available and costs slightly less per unit, and usually more per pallet once freight is in.

Are the corners really dovetailed?

Yes, machine-cut and visible on every face. It is the detail a craft buyer photographs, and it is why this blank sells at a premium over a stapled box.

Can you stain or seal them for us?

Yes, though most personalisation buyers would rather do it themselves for control. If you want it done here we will match a colour reference and batch it so the whole run is consistent.

title: Wooden Countertop Cabinet with Fluted Glass Doors — Router and AV Storage Cabinet
content:
Introduction: A low wooden cabinet with twin fluted glass doors, sized to sit on a sideboard, desk or shelf. It exists to hide the equipment nobody wants to look at — a router, a set-top box, a modem, a charging tangle — while the ribbed glass diffuses the view and, critically, does not block wireless signal the way a metal enclosure would.

Key Features

  • Fluted glass doors: the contents are obscured, not sealed away, so status lights still read and signal passes through
  • Cable exits at the rear, cut on both sides so the unit works against a wall or in a corner
  • Ventilation gaps top and rear — concealed electronics that cannot breathe are concealed electronics that fail
  • Rustic stained solid-wood carcass with a flat top rated to take a lamp, a plant or a speaker
  • Magnetic door catches and turned knobs; doors open past 100 degrees for access
  • Interior shelf optional, to stack a router above a modem

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to homeware and interiors retailers, home-office and DTC brands, marketplace sellers, and hospitality suppliers fitting out serviced apartments. Serviced apartments and boutique hotels are an underrated buyer — guest-facing routers are ugly and unavoidable, and a wooden cabinet solves it without a joinery project.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Ventilation is the specification people forget. A router in a sealed box runs hot, throttles, and the customer blames the cabinet. We cut gaps top and rear as standard and we will not remove them for a cleaner look. Send us the actual equipment dimensions including the antennas at their widest, and tell us whether it sits against a wall or free-standing.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

Will it block the wifi signal?

Glass and wood do not block wifi the way metal does, so the practical answer is no. If the router has external antennas they should stay outside or the cabinet should be sized so they stand upright inside; send us the model and we will size it.

Does the equipment overheat?

Not with the ventilation gaps we cut as standard. We will not delete them for a cleaner look, because a throttled router is the complaint this product generates and the gaps are what prevent it.

Can we have plain glass instead of fluted?

Yes, and also smoked or frosted. Fluted is the current favourite because it hides cable clutter while still letting light and status lights through; plain glass shows everything, which defeats the point for most buyers.

How big can it be?

As large as you need, but past a certain width we would add a centre stile so the doors do not sag. Tell us the equipment and the shelf it has to sit on and we will draw it.

Can it be wall-mounted?

Yes, with keyhole hangers or a French cleat. Say so at quotation, because a wall-mounted version needs a stronger back panel than a countertop one and it is easier to build in than to add later.

How do I know it is solid walnut and not veneer?

Look into a cut slot. On solid timber the grain continues through the thickness; on veneered MDF you see the core. It is the check we would make on a competitor's sample and it is why we cut the slots the way we do.

Why no hinge on the lid?

Because a hinge stops the lid opening flat and gets in the way when you are rewiring, which is the only time the box is ever opened. A lift-off lid also removes the one part that could ever loosen.

  • Cable slots front and side, with a routed channel guiding leads up through the top
  • Bamboo throughout — light, stable, and a defensible sustainability line for your listing
  • A configurable product photographs endlessly: every use case is a different image from one SKU
  • Dowels are a consumable we can resupply, not a proprietary part

Specifications

Sold to desk-accessory and DTC brands, marketplace sellers, corporate-gift programmes, and electronics-accessory retailers. Marketplace sellers do particularly well with it because a configurable product generates a dozen distinct listing images from one unit, and image volume is what moves a listing in this category.

Peg count and hole pitch are the two numbers worth thinking about. A tighter pitch gives finer control and weakens the top; ours is set where it holds. Do the dowels hold firmly?

Yes, at the hole pitch and fit we specify. A looser fit makes them easy to move and too easy to knock out; we set it so they stay where they are put but come out by hand. You will feel it on the sample.

Can we include spare dowels?

Yes, and we recommend it. They cost almost nothing and they are the part that gets lost. A customer who loses two and cannot replace them stops using the station, and that is a review you do not want.

Can the peg layout be pre-set for a particular device?

It can, but the selling point is that the user sets it. If you are doing a bundled corporate gift with one device in mind, we will ship it pre-configured with a card showing how to change it.

Is bamboo strong enough for a drilled top?

Yes — laminated moso bamboo is dimensionally very stable and takes a drilled array without the hole edges breaking out, which is a real risk in softwood. It is the right material for this specific product.

Can we add wireless charging?

We do not build electronics, and we would not want to be the reason a certification lapses. What we can do is cut a recess and a cable channel for a module you supply or specify, and we will build the sample around the actual module.

Will it affect the wifi signal?

Antennas stand upright through the roof slots and the back is open, so in practice no. Folding antennas down inside a closed box is what degrades signal, and this design specifically avoids it.

Can we put our own name on the front?

content:
Introduction: A set of walnut jewelry display risers — flat plinths and raised tiers that combine into a stepped arrangement on a counter or inside a showcase. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. Tell us the internal dimensions of your showcase. Risers that leave an awkward gap look worse than no risers, and the whole set should divide cleanly into the shelf. If you are rolling out across stores, order components rather than sets — different store formats need different mixes and a fixed set forces you to buy pieces you will not use.

Can we buy individual pieces instead of the set?

Yes, and for a multi-store rollout you should. Store formats differ and a fixed set means buying components you will not use. We quote each part separately for exactly this reason.

Bare wood or covered tops?

Bare walnut for a warm, design-led look; micro-suede or felt facing if the pieces are delicate or if you want a colour to sit behind them. We will send one of each on the sample.

Will they fit our showcase?

Send the internal length, width and height. We size the set so a whole number of pieces fills the shelf — a riser set that leaves a 4 cm gap at one end undoes the tidiness it was bought for.

title: Hexagon Wooden Display Risers — Solid Wood Block Stands for Product Photography
content:
Introduction: A set of six solid hexagonal display risers in graduated heights, in a dark rustic oak finish. They are display blocks in the plainest sense — no felt, no cloth, no hardware — and they sell to two distinct buyers for the same reason: they lift a product to a useful height and they look like nothing, which is exactly what a display prop should do.

  • Solid timber, not hollow boxes — they have weight, which is what stops a display shifting when a customer picks something up
  • Dark rustic oak finish as shown; any stain, plus white and black for e-commerce photography
  • No felt or cloth to date or wear; the whole point is a surface that stays neutral
  • Sold as a set or in single heights

Specifications

Who Buys This

Sold to visual-merchandising and shopfitting suppliers, cosmetics and skincare brands, product-photography studios and e-commerce sellers, and craft and candle brands. E-commerce photography is the growth side: every seller needs to stage product shots, and a set of neutral wooden blocks is the cheapest professional-looking answer there is.

Customisation

Every item here is made to order in our own factory. Wood species, stain colour, dimensions, hardware finish and packaging are all open to change. Logo options are laser engraving, gold- silver- or copper-fill laser engraving, UV printing and screen printing — we do not offer hot foil or embossing on wood, because neither bonds reliably to open grain. If these are for photography, order the white and the black sets as well as the wood — sellers shoot against all three grounds and a wood-only set limits them. If they are for retail display, match the stain to your fixtures and send a physical sample to match against rather than a screen colour.

Quality Control

All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Solid or hollow?

Solid. Hollow boxes are cheaper and lighter and they skid across a counter the moment a customer lifts the product off them. The weight is the feature here, not an accident.

Why hexagonal rather than round or square?

The flats let blocks sit against each other with no gap, so a group of six reads as one honeycomb arrangement. Round blocks leave crescents of empty counter between them and square ones look like a grid.

Yes, and for photography buyers we recommend taking all three. Sellers shoot on different grounds and a wood-only set restricts them to one look.

Will the finish mark under hot lights?

Not at studio distances with LED lighting, which is what everybody uses now. Under old tungsten hot lights held close, any finish will eventually suffer; we use a hard stain-and-seal rather than a wax for this reason.

Yes. Beyond about 25 cm a solid block gets heavy and expensive and we would hollow the core while keeping a weighted base, which we will tell you rather than quietly switching construction.

Not with slot-together joinery cut to a tight fit, which is what we do. Flat-pack fails when it relies on screws into end grain; interlocking slots put the load on the material instead.

title: Bamboo Angled Document Tray — 2-Tier Sloped Paper and File Tray for Desks
content:
Introduction: A bamboo document tray with a sloped wedge profile, supplied as two stackable tiers. The angle is the entire idea: in a flat tray the top sheet is the only thing you can see and the pile below is invisible, whereas a sloped tray steps the contents so the labels and titles stay readable without lifting anything out.

  • Sloped wedge profile — contents step forward so titles and tabs stay visible
  • Stacks cleanly on posts, two or three high, without the tiers wandering
  • Open front and side, so a document slides out without being lifted over a rim
  • Solid bamboo panels with visible node pattern, sealed matte
  • No metal posts to bend or lose — the spacers are turned wood
  • Nests flat for shipping, which is what keeps freight sane on a bulky shape

Sold to office-supply distributors, desk-accessory and DTC brands, marketplace sellers, and corporate procurement. Office-supply distributors are the steady channel because a paper tray is a repeat consumable purchase in a way that most wooden desk accessories are not.

Specify the paper size for the market. A4 and US Letter are different enough that a tray sized for one holds the other badly, and this is the most common avoidable error in desk filing products. All timber ships at 8–12% moisture content, measured after kilning and again before packing, with the reading stated on the packing list. That single specification decides whether a wooden product arrives flat or cupped after six weeks in a container. Every unit is checked for glue squeeze-out, sanding grade and finish evenness before it is cartoned, and we photograph a random pull from each packed lot so you see the goods as they actually left the line.

Frequently Asked Questions

A4 or Letter?

Specify at order. They are different enough that a tray cut for one is visibly wrong for the other, and it is the error we see most often when a buyer reuses a spec across markets.

How high can it stack?

Three tiers comfortably. Beyond that the stack gets top-heavy and a document pulled from the bottom tier tips it, so we cap the posts we supply at three.

Why wooden spacers instead of metal posts?

Metal posts bend, get lost and look like office furniture from 1995. Turned wood posts match the tray, cannot bend, and are cheap to replace if one goes missing.

Does bamboo mark from paper dye?

Sealed bamboo does not. Raw bamboo can pick up colour from a wet printed sheet left on it, which is why we seal it and why we would not quote an unsealed version for this product.

Can we brand it?

Laser engraving on the side panel, which stays visible when the tray is loaded. Engraving on the deck disappears under the first document.

The located groove. Most wooden trays rest flat on each other and drift apart as documents are pulled; ours seats into the rim below so the stack stays square. It is the only functional difference in this category and it is worth saying so in your listing.

Four comfortably. Higher and the top tray is above comfortable reach on a standard desk, which is a usability limit rather than a structural one.

If they are ordered together and you tell us, yes — we batch the timber. Ordered separately they will be close but not identical. Walnut varies board to board and no honest supplier can promise otherwise across separate runs.

Oil as standard, because an executive desk tray gets marked and an oiled surface is repairable where lacquer chips. If it is going into a high-traffic shared office we will quote lacquer instead and say why.

Three comfortably. The rim locates rather than just resting, so the stack stays square, but above three the top tray is an awkward reach on a standard desk.

Is there a cheaper wood?

Oak and cherry run on the same tooling at a lower price, and bamboo lower again. For the executive-desk buyer the walnut is the point, so we would not steer you off it — but for a volume line, the same tray in oak is a legitimate product.

Width. A wire divider is a few millimetres thick where a wooden one is ten or more, so you get five slots in the space that would otherwise hold three. On a desk, that difference is the whole product.

Metal and wood run on separate lead times and the frame has to be made before it can be fitted to the base. Plan 14-18 days rather than a week; production is a similar step up.

Onions and potatoes stored together spoil noticeably faster — the onions give off moisture and gas that sprouts the potatoes. A divider is a few cents of bamboo that solves a real kitchen problem, and it is worth saying so in your listing.
